title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is at a crossroads, balancing ambitious hiring against the weight of legacy systems. Meanwhile, new technologies and collaborations are emerging, hinting at a future where space is both a battleground and a marketplace.

themes.title: Hiring vs. Heritage
themes.body: The space sector is grappling with the challenge of expanding its workforce while still relying on established practices and personnel. This tension could either stifle innovation or push companies to rethink their operational models.

themes.title: Nuclear Batteries in Orbit
themes.body: A startup's foray into nuclear battery technology could redefine power sources for satellites, assuming it doesn't become a political hot potato. The implications for long-duration missions are tantalizing, if not a bit radioactive.

themes.title: China's Orbital Milestone
themes.body: China's recovery of its Long March 10B booster marks a significant step in its reusable launch capabilities, placing it firmly in the space race. This achievement could shift the competitive dynamics, especially for those still clinging to traditional launch methods.

themes.title: Defense-Tech IPO Buzz
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window is showing signs of life, but investors will need more than just a good story to commit capital. With the buzz around AI and space resilience, the real question is whether these companies can deliver on their promises.
